html:
RoMa (2024): dense matching between two photos of one scene from any viewpoints: where each pixel of the first image is in the second, and how sure the model is that it is visible there. Built on Meta's DINOv2 and a VGG19. MIT code and weights; the DINOv2 weights are Apache-2.0.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Paper: RoMa: Robust Dense Feature Matching, CVPR 2024, 2023-05-24
  • Original code: https://github.com/Parskatt/RoMa at 77f8d6880352
  • Code licence: MIT (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: MIT AND Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/Parskatt/RoMa/blob/77f8d68803526dcddfd9b7a46bc76125bdc25f15/README.md#license
  • Training data: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth) (roma_outdoor: MegaDepth (upstream README / paper). The frozen DINOv2 was pretrained on LVD-142M (not released).)
  • Licence note: The DINOv2 ViT-L/14 weights are the second weight file (Meta's release, Apache-2.0).
  • Options: coarse_size = 560 (>= 14), fine_size = 864 (>= 0)
  • Kernel libraries: fastbb
  • Variants: romav1
  • Outputs: warp, certainty
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): romav1 3000x4000 (1.9 GiB peak allocated, 2.2 reserved)
  • romav1 original 768x1024: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream RoMa v1 match, one direction; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (use_custom_corr off)
  • romav1 load / first call: original 6.28 s / 2.57 s, portable 1.09 s / 0.834 s, kernels 1.96 s / 0.862 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 4.3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.00079 and p99 <= 0.0042 (absolute error of the output warp).

Limitations

  • One direction (the first image's half of upstream's symmetric call); upstream's sampling / keypoint helpers are not included; tools/eval_matching.py has the MegaDepth-1500 sampling.
  • Both images are resized to squares (upstream's behaviour), whatever their aspect ratio; upstream resizes PIL images, this runner float tensors (bicubic, antialiased).
